text.arabic_uthmani: فَتَرَى ٱلَّذِينَ فِى قُلُوبِهِم مَّرَضٌۭ يُسَٰرِعُونَ فِيهِمْ يَقُولُونَ نَخْشَىٰٓ أَن تُصِيبَنَا دَآئِرَةٌۭ ۚ فَعَسَى ٱللَّهُ أَن يَأْتِىَ بِٱلْفَتْحِ أَوْ أَمْرٍۢ مِّنْ عِندِهِۦ فَيُصْبِحُوا۟ عَلَىٰ مَآ أَسَرُّوا۟ فِىٓ أَنفُسِهِمْ نَٰدِمِينَ

words.gloss_range: resumptive and consequential connector opening the observed scene
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) carries the warning of 5:51 into a visible scene. The opening connector makes the observation feel consequential, and the repeated connector pattern divides the ayah into observation, divine counter-possibility, and resulting regret.

topics.headline: opening consequence from the prior boundary
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the scene as the visible outcome of the prior boundary warning in 5:51, not as a detached report.
topics.reason: QAC identifies the particle as a connector, and the boundary rows tie the opening observation to the prior prohibition.

topics.headline: repeated pivot cadence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the ayah moving through a staged sequence: observation, divine response, then consequence.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows identify the three connector pivots and the four-beat movement they create.

words.gloss_range: ongoing second-person perception that presents the group under observation
words.root_gloss_range: seeing, perceiving, judging; dream-vision remains outside the local force
words.prose: {{ar:تَرَى}} ({{tr:tarā}}) puts the addressee in the position of an ongoing witness: the group and its rushing are seen as evidence in process. The root range allows perception and judgment, while the local form keeps dream-vision outside the active sense; the variant shifts the observer into a more detached third-person frame. The same seeing-hastening frame returns in Surah 5 (5:62), and the scene layers from witness, to their speech, to God’s counter-action.

topics.headline: ongoing observed object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the disease-hearted conduct is displayed under continuing observation rather than merely reported.
topics.reason: QAC marks a second-person imperfect perception verb governing the relative group as its observed object.

topics.headline: sight plus judgment, not dream-vision
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can keep both seeing and discernment in view without importing dream-vision into the local scene.
topics.reason: The root range includes physical sight, judgment, and dream-vision, but local syntax is direct observation of a social scene.

topics.headline: direct address strengthened by variant contrast
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the standard reading makes the witness directly addressed, while the variant shows that observer position is interpretively live.
topics.reason: The accepted variant can illuminate observer position, but the canonical local wording remains second-person address.

topics.headline: seeing-hastening echo (5:62)
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes a same-surah diagnostic frame in which seeing and hastening expose corrupt motion (5:62).
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows give the concrete same-surah parallel at 5:62.

topics.headline: observer, speakers, and divine response
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the scene open from witness, to their speech, to God’s counter-action.
topics.reason: The row cluster tracks the ayah-level layering and the opening sound shape.

words.gloss_range: relative pronoun defining the observed group by its inner condition
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلَّذِينَ}} ({{tr:alladhīna}}) does not label the actors first; it makes them a relative group whose identity is completed by what follows. The syntax delays the main rushing predicate so the reader receives inner diagnosis before outward action.

topics.headline: relative definition before action
topics.reader_payoff: The reader identifies the group by its diagnosed condition before seeing its behavior.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence identify the relative pronoun as the object of perception, completed by the following diagnostic relative clause.

words.gloss_range: locative preposition that makes the heart a diagnostic container
words.prose: {{ar:فِى}} ({{tr:fī}}) makes the first diagnosis locative: the pathology is inside hearts before any external movement appears. That interior placement also begins the frame that closes later inside selves, and the nasal binding around the phrase helps the opening interior feel held together.

topics.headline: hearts as disease container
topics.reader_payoff: The reader enters the ayah through an inner container rather than through visible behavior.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence make the preposition govern the heart phrase, and the CRITICAL rows preserve the locative diagnostic formula.

topics.headline: opening interior frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears and tracks the opening interior phrase as the first half of an inside-to-inside frame.
topics.reason: The row cluster connects the opening locative diagnosis with the later closing interior phrase and notes the local sound binding.

words.gloss_range: possessed plural hearts as distributed inner decision centers
words.root_gloss_range: turning/reversal, heart, cognitive and volitional center
words.prose: {{ar:قُلُوبِهِم}} ({{tr:qulūbihim}}) is plural and possessed, so the disease is distributed through their own inner centers. The root field of turning makes those centers unstable, and the phrase participates in the recognized disease-in-hearts formula (2:10) and the same-surah heart diagnosis at 5:41, while the ayah later answers it with concealed selves.

topics.headline: distributed possessed hearts

topics.headline: turning cognitive center

topics.reason: The V4/root evidence supports heart as cognitive-volitional center and the CRITICAL rows tie the turning image to the ayah’s reversal arc.

topics.headline: disease-in-hearts formula (2:10; 5:41)

topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows provide formula parallels at 2:10 and 5:41.

topics.headline: heart-to-self interior ring
topics.reader_payoff: The reader follows the ayah from diseased hearts to exposed selves, with turning and opening images crossing the frame.
topics.reason: The local word participates in the ayah’s opening and closing interior frame and in the root-image contrast with the feared turn.

words.gloss_range: indefinite inner disease as broad moral and epistemic pathology
words.root_gloss_range: sickness, weakness, doubt, corruption; physical illness is metaphorical here
words.prose: {{ar:مَّرَضٌۭ}} ({{tr:maraḍun}}) is indefinite, so the condition remains broad rather than a named illness. The sickness metaphor makes the subsequent rushing a symptom of compromised inner function, and the disease-in-hearts formula is specialized here by visible alliance movement. The geminated onset gives the diagnosis a compressed audible weight.

topics.headline: unspecified diagnostic disease

topics.reason: QAC marks the word as nominative indefinite, and CRITICAL rows stress the diagnostic breadth of tanwīn.

topics.headline: moral-epistemic sickness
topics.reader_payoff: The reader treats the rush as pathology rather than ordinary political caution, with 2:10 providing formula background.
topics.reason: V4 and contextual rows support sickness as a metaphor for doubt or corruption, and the local clause shows the behavioral symptom.

topics.headline: compressed disease sound
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the word enter with weight that matches the obstructive diagnostic load.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL sound rows connect the geminated onset and indefinite diagnosis to local effect.

words.gloss_range: ongoing plural hastening with competitive or intensive force
words.root_gloss_range: speed, haste, striving; locally social movement into an alliance sphere
words.prose: {{ar:يُسَٰرِعُونَ}} ({{tr:yusāriʿūna}}) presents ongoing group motion, and its Form III profile makes the haste feel socially charged and competitive, not merely quick. The complement that follows directs that speed into the other group’s sphere, while the same Surah 5 hastening pattern links it to compromised alignment (5:41). Its shared plural cadence with the speech and becoming verbs binds action, explanation, and consequence into one behavioral package.

topics.reason: QAC identifies the verb as imperfect plural, and form rows preserve the Form III competitive or intensive profile.

topics.headline: haste completed by its target

topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the following prepositional phrase the complement of the rushing verb.

topics.headline: Surah 5 hastening profile (5:41)
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears this rush inside a same-surah pattern where hastening marks compromised movement (5:41).
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows give concrete same-surah parallels for the hastening field.

topics.headline: action before speech with shared cadence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears action and explanation as one behavioral package.
topics.reason: The rows connect the plural imperfect cadence and the later speech frame.

words.gloss_range: preposition plus pronoun marking the alliance target as among or toward them
words.prose: {{ar:فِيهِمْ}} ({{tr:fīhim}}) is the referential hinge back to 5:51: the pronoun points to the previously named groups. The preposition leaves both among and toward active, so the rush can be heard as entry into their sphere and movement in their direction. The final nasal pronoun makes the haste phrase audibly land on that target.

topics.headline: pronoun carried from 5:51

topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows and contextual boundary evidence tie the suffix to the prior named groups.

topics.headline: among and toward kept live

topics.reason: The preposition with a human pronoun can sustain locative and directional readings, and the syntax completes the rushing verb.

topics.headline: from identity absorption to movement into them
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees 5:51’s warning about becoming of them become visible as rushing into their sphere in 5:52.
topics.reason: The boundary rows compare the repeated pronoun across 5:51 and 5:52.

topics.headline: closed destination sound
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the haste phrase land on its pronoun target.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL row gives a local sound payoff for the suffix ending.

words.gloss_range: ongoing plural saying that supplies a contemporaneous justification
words.root_gloss_range: saying, claiming, uttering; locally their public rationale
words.prose: {{ar:يَقُولُونَ}} ({{tr:yaqūlūna}}) makes their excuse contemporaneous with their rushing: they are moving while saying. The speech externalizes part of the inner calculation, but the later perfect concealment shows that the public explanation does not exhaust what they hid. The repeated plural cadence carries the same group through action, speech, and consequence.

topics.headline: saying as circumstantial excuse
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears their statement as the caption to their behavior, not as an unrelated remark.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence treats the speech as a circumstantial clause accompanying the hastening.

topics.headline: public speech versus hidden calculation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the contrast between what they keep saying and what they had already concealed.
topics.reason: The tense contrast between ongoing speech and later perfect concealment supports the disclosure payoff.

topics.headline: contested speech thread (5:41; 5:53)
topics.reader_payoff: The reader locates this excuse within Surah 5’s wider pattern of exposed claims and later evaluation (5:41; 5:53).
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows cite concrete same-surah speech links at 5:41 and 5:53.

topics.headline: plural action-speech cadence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the same group carried through action, speech, and consequence.
topics.reason: The sound row links the plural endings across the ayah.

words.gloss_range: first-person plural fear governing a feared-event clause
words.root_gloss_range: fear with awareness or awe; locally misdirected toward reversal rather than God
words.prose: {{ar:نَخْشَىٰٓ}} ({{tr:nakhshā}}) gives the quote a collective voice: their rhetoric is we-fear, and it governs the following feared-event clause as a specific scenario. What makes the fear self-indicting is its object; Surah 5 commands fear toward God (5:3; 5:44), while this speech directs the fear-register toward a worldly reversal. The guttural onset gives the utterance a constricted anxious sound.

topics.headline: collective fear rhetoric
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears a group policy presented as prudent shared fear.
topics.reason: QAC marks a first-person plural imperfect inside the direct quote.

topics.headline: fear governs a specific event
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that their fear is not vague anxiety but a structured feared scenario.
topics.reason: The verb governs the following subordinated feared-event clause.

topics.headline: fear-object inversion (5:3; 5:44)
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that a fear-register commanded toward God elsewhere in Surah 5 is redirected here toward reversal (5:3; 5:44).
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows cite the concrete Surah 5 commands that expose the wrong object of fear.

topics.headline: rough fear onset
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears anxiety in the constricted onset of the quoted verb.
topics.reason: The sound row supplies the local phonetic payoff.

words.gloss_range: subordinating particle packaging the feared event as possibility
words.prose: {{ar:أَن}} ({{tr:an}}) turns the next clause into the content of fear. The event remains possible and dreaded, not accomplished, and the small nasal particle binds the fear verb to the imagined strike and to the following us-object.

topics.headline: feared event as subordinate possibility

topics.reason: QAC marks the particle as introducing a subjunctive content clause.

topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the particle bind into the following first-person object.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL sound row notes the nasal link into the following verb.

words.gloss_range: subjunctive strike or befalling with the speakers as object
words.root_gloss_range: hitting the mark, correctness, affliction; locally a feared impact
words.prose: {{ar:تُصِيبَنَا}} ({{tr:tuṣībanā}}) makes the feared turn the grammatical striker and the speakers the patients of impact. The root range adds a sharp irony: what befalls can also be what hits the mark, while 5:49 reverses the striking perspective from divine warning into their anxious self-protection. The ayah later redirects the real impact into regret, and the emphatic sound gives the feared blow a focused edge.

topics.headline: feminine subject strikes the speakers
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the feared reversal as an agentive incoming blow aimed at them.
topics.reason: QAC identifies the verb as feminine subjunctive agreeing with the following feminine subject and carrying the attached first-person object.

topics.headline: being struck and hitting the mark
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears their feared affliction as something that may land with precision, not random noise.
topics.reason: V4/root rows preserve the field of befalling, impact, and correctness.

topics.headline: striking perspective reversed (5:49)
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees their self-protective fear answer an earlier divine warning, while the actual consequence becomes regret (5:49).
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows cite 5:49 and compare the feared strike with the later regret result.

topics.headline: focused impact sound
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears a focused impact in the word’s emphatic sound shape.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL sound row supplies the phonetic effect.

words.gloss_range: indefinite turn of fortune acting as the feared striker
words.root_gloss_range: circling, turning, reversal, calamity; locally an adverse cycle
words.prose: {{ar:دَآئِرَةٌۭ}} ({{tr:dāʾiratun}}) is the subject they fear: a turn of fortune that might strike them. Its root image keeps circling and reversal alive, the indefinite form leaves the danger unspecified, and the rare negative cycle field makes their alliance motive sound like anxiety before fortune’s wheel, with 9:98 giving a concrete adverse-cycle parallel. The irony is that turning hearts fear a turning cycle, and the long opening sound lets that feared turn feel extended.

topics.headline: turn of fortune as subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the motive behind the alliance rush: fear of an unspecified reversal that might hit them.
topics.reason: QAC and CRITICAL rows identify the noun as the nominative subject of the feared strike and as indefinite.

topics.headline: cycle and calamity held together
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears calamity as a turning cycle, not a flat synonym for misfortune, with 9:98 as a concrete adverse-cycle parallel.
topics.reason: V4/root and CRITICAL rows support the turn/cycle image and cite 9:98.

topics.headline: turning hearts fear a turning cycle
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the irony that unstable hearts fear an external turn while the ayah exposes an inward cycle.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows connect the feared cycle with the earlier heart-turning image.

topics.headline: stretched turn sound
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the feared turn lengthened rather than clipped.
topics.reason: The sound row gives the acoustic effect of the long opening.

words.gloss_range: central pivot particle from human projection to divine counter-action
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) is the ayah’s central hinge. It moves out of their quoted fear and opens the divine counter-clause, so the second half is not governed by their projection but by what God may bring. As the middle connector, it echoes the opening hinge and prepares the final consequence hinge.

topics.headline: human fear to divine initiative

topics.reason: Attachment and discourse rows identify the particle as the pivot out of the quote into the divine response clause.

topics.headline: middle connector in repeated pivot chain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the middle hinge echo the opening and prepare the final consequence connector.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL sound row connects this particle to the ayah’s repeated pivot cadence.

words.gloss_range: modal hope or expectation introducing divine counter-possibility
words.root_gloss_range: hope, expectation; with divine subject it leans toward assured action
words.prose: {{ar:عَسَى}} ({{tr:ʿasā}}) reopens the future against their anxious certainty. As a modal verb with God as subject, it carries hope or expectation that leans toward assured divine action, and its divine-bringing construction has a concrete hope-formula parallel at 12:83. Its long ending audibly answers the long ending of their fear verb.

topics.headline: modal frame for divine outcome
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears possibility shift from what they fear to what God may decisively do.
topics.reason: QAC and grammar rows identify the modal construction and its divine subject as the opening of the counter-possibility.

topics.headline: divine bringing hope formula (12:83)
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes a divine-bringing hope formula with 12:83 as a concrete parallel.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows cite the constructional parallel at 12:83.

topics.headline: long vowel answer to fear

words.gloss_range: proper divine subject of the counter-clause
words.root_gloss_range: divine name field; local force is the proper divine subject, not a generic noun
words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهُ}} ({{tr:Allāhu}}) supplies the subject of the counter-possibility: God, not the feared turn, becomes the active center. The divine name also restores the proper pole of fear against the misdirected fear voiced earlier in the quote (5:44), while the worship-and-attachment pressure remains narrowed to the proper-name role. The same divine counter-action also sits near the becoming-regret echo of 5:31, and the liaison makes the modal frame audibly bind to the divine subject.

topics.headline: modal bound to divine subject

Its openness matters because the ayah moves from a known decisive opening to any source-marked action God may send from His domain, with concrete divine-command parallels at 2:109 and 9:24. The tanwīn runs into the following source phrase, making the unspecified command audibly attach to its provenance.

topics.headline: source phrase clings by sound
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the source phrase bind tightly to the indefinite command.
topics.reason: The sound row notes the nasal bridge from the command noun into the source preposition.

words.gloss_range: suffixed proximity noun marking source from God’s own domain
words.root_gloss_range: nearness, presence, possession, jurisdiction; locally divine provenance
words.prose: {{ar:عِنْدِهِۦ}} ({{tr:ʿindihī}}) seals the source phrase with a suffixed reference back to God. The word carries nearness, possession, and jurisdiction, so the unspecified command is not vague fate; it comes from His own domain, with 6:59 giving a concrete possession formula parallel.

topics.headline: personal divine source
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the unspecified command made personally and compactly God-sourced.
topics.reason: QAC and CRITICAL rows tie the suffix back to the divine subject and show the source phrase sealing the second alternative.

topics.headline: presence and possession as authority
topics.reader_payoff: The reader senses provenance as nearness and possession, not abstract authorization.
topics.reason: V4/root rows support the presence, possession, and jurisdiction range.

topics.headline: divine possession parallel (6:59)
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can hear the source phrase in a broader divine possession field, with 6:59 as a concrete parallel.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows cite 6:59 and connect the source noun to opening and command fields.

words.gloss_range: consequential connector linking divine action to resulting regret
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) makes the final state consequential. The regret that follows is not an incidental emotion but the result downstream of divine opening or command, completing the connector chain that began the ayah.

topics.headline: divine action to regret consequence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees regret as the outcome of divine intervention, not as a separate emotional episode.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence identify the connector as consequential before the becoming verb.

topics.headline: final connector in pivot chain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the ayah’s last turn from possibility into consequence.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows tie this connector to the repeated pivot sequence.

words.gloss_range: subjunctive becoming with dawn-exposure resonance
words.root_gloss_range: morning, becoming, entering a state; locally exposure into regret
words.prose: {{ar:يُصْبِحُوا۟}} ({{tr:yuṣbiḥū}}) keeps the regret inside the modal outcome chain and casts it as a state they enter. Because the becoming verb carries morning and exposure resonance, the hidden interior reaches daylight; the same becoming-regret formula appears earlier in Surah 5 (5:31). The long plural ending links what they become to the earlier plural concealment.

topics.headline: becoming as result state
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees regret as a state entered through the divine-response chain, not as another action they perform.
topics.reason: QAC and CRITICAL rows identify the verb as subjunctive within the modal chain and as a copula of becoming.

topics.headline: morning exposure undoes secrecy
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels hidden calculation brought into daylight as regret.
topics.reason: V4/root and CRITICAL rows preserve the morning/light exposure image and its opposition to concealment.

topics.headline: becoming-regret formula (5:31)
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the disease-hearted future regret resonate with the same-surah remorse formula at 5:31.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows cite the concrete 5:31 parallel.

topics.headline: long plural sound links concealment and becoming
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears what they concealed linked to what they become.
topics.reason: The sound row connects the long plural ending here with the concealment verb.

words.gloss_range: preposition marking the domain on which regret rests
words.prose: {{ar:عَلَىٰ}} ({{tr:ʿalā}}) marks what regret rests upon: the concealed content. The spatial force of upon gives remorse weight, and the phrase naming the domain of regret comes before the final regret predicate lands. The long held sound opens the movement into that concealed content.

topics.headline: domain and cause of regret
topics.reader_payoff: The reader knows what the final regret is about before the regret word arrives.
topics.reason: QAC marks the preposition as governing the concealed-content clause and CRITICAL rows note its placement before the predicate.

topics.headline: regret bears down upon concealment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels remorse as weight landing on the hidden matter.
topics.reason: The preposition’s spatial force supports the figurative weight image.

topics.headline: long held regret-domain phrase
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the phrase slow as it enters the hidden content.
topics.reason: The sound row notes the long vowel bridge into the following relative particle.

words.gloss_range: relative particle leaving the concealed content unnamed
words.prose: {{ar:مَآ}} ({{tr:mā}}) leaves the concealed content unnamed. It opens a relative slot wide enough for motive, alliance, calculation, or fear, making the final regret fall on a whole hidden proposition rather than a single specified object. Its long vowel bridges the regret-domain phrase into the concealment verb.

topics.headline: open relative object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the secret is grammatically present but deliberately unspecified.
topics.reason: QAC marks the particle as a relative pronoun introducing the concealed-content clause.

topics.headline: smooth bridge into concealment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the regret-domain phrase flow into the concealment verb as one unit.
topics.reason: The sound row notes the vowel bridge from the preposition to the concealment verb.

words.gloss_range: completed plural concealment as enacted secrecy before exposure
words.root_gloss_range: secret, concealment, inner enclosure; reveal-sense is contrastive, not the selected local sense
words.prose: {{ar:أَسَرُّوا۟}} ({{tr:asarrū}}) is perfect plural, so the concealment is already complete before the becoming-regret result. Its local sense is enacted secrecy, while the wider root field allows a narrowed exposure irony and even hidden investment that reverses into remorse: the verb of hiding stands inside an ayah where God’s opening will reveal what was sealed. The concealment-in-self idiom has a contrasting parallel at 12:77, and the geminated sound compresses the secrecy at the point it is named.

topics.headline: completed group concealment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees regret rest on a prior completed act of collective concealment.
topics.reason: QAC marks a perfect plural verb, and CRITICAL rows note its governing relation to the relative content and locative frame.

topics.headline: secret enclosure before opening
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the hidden material as sealed interior content that the divine opening will unseal.
topics.reason: Root and structural rows directly oppose secrecy to the opening field.

topics.headline: hidden investment and reveal-sense pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can sense hidden investment and exposure irony, while the local selected meaning remains concealment.
topics.reason: The broader root and contronym evidence is valid, but local syntax selects hiding rather than revealing.

topics.headline: concealment and regret parallels (12:77)
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can compare diseased concealment here with a contrasting concealment-in-self scene at 12:77.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows cite 12:77 and the secrecy-regret pairing.

topics.headline: tightened secrecy sound
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears concealment compressed at the point where secrecy is named.
topics.reason: The sound row notes the geminated consonant effect.

words.gloss_range: locative preposition placing concealment inside the selves
words.prose: {{ar:فِىٓ}} ({{tr:fī}}) locates the concealment inside their selves. As the second locative interior marker, it answers the opening inside-hearts phrase and helps frame the whole ayah as outward motion enclosed by inward diagnosis and inward exposure. The nasal cluster around the self phrase deepens the inward closure.

topics.headline: secrecy inside selves
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the self as the storage site of the hidden calculation.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence identify the preposition as governing the selves phrase.

topics.headline: second interior locative returns to the opening
topics.reader_payoff: The reader follows an interior frame from hearts at the beginning to selves near the end.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows explicitly connect the two locative interior phrases.

topics.headline: nasal inward closure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the closing interior phrase turn inward.
topics.reason: The sound row notes the nasal cluster around the self word.

words.gloss_range: possessed plural selves as the inner site of hidden calculation
words.root_gloss_range: self, soul, personhood, appetite, agency; locally total inward personhood
words.prose: {{ar:أَنفُسِهِمْ}} ({{tr:anfusihim}}) makes the hidden site their own selves, not merely an external alliance. The word broadens the interior field from heart to whole personhood and agency, with breath-and-competition pressure kept only as a faint root-family resonance. The closing frame turns social exposure into self-exposure, with 12:77 as a contrasting concealment-in-self parallel.

topics.headline: their own selves as hidden site
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the hidden matter lodged in their own distributed selves before regret lands.
topics.reason: QAC marks a plural noun with possessive suffix immediately before the final predicate.

topics.headline: self beyond heart
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the ayah move from diseased organ to whole inner personhood and agency.
topics.reason: V4/root rows support self, soul, will, and personhood, and CRITICAL rows contrast this with the opening heart term.

topics.headline: self-field touches breath and competition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader may hear a faint link between self, breath, and striving, while local grammar selects selves as the site of concealment.
topics.reason: The broader root-family pressure is suggestive, but the local noun functions as the concealed location.

topics.headline: contrastive concealment-in-self parallel (12:77)
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can compare this corrupt concealment with a contrasting concealment-in-self idiom at 12:77.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows cite the concrete 12:77 parallel.

topics.headline: hearts return as selves at closure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the ayah’s social plot resolve as interior self-exposure.
topics.reason: The rows connect the opening heart phrase, the closing self phrase, and the prior boundary verdict.

words.gloss_range: plural active-participle regret as the resulting state
words.root_gloss_range: remorse and regret after recognition; locally an abiding group state
words.prose: {{ar:نَٰدِمِينَ}} ({{tr:nādimīna}}) is the final state they become: plural, participial, and ongoing regret. The word closes the ayah by turning hidden fear-driven strategy into exposed remorse, while the becoming-regret formula recalls 5:31 and the next ayah’s speech will interpret this exposed state (5:53). The variant lightens the vocalic weight without changing the predicate role, and the final sound settles earlier uncertainty into remorse.

topics.headline: regret as becoming predicate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees regret as an abiding group condition entered through the previous verb.
topics.reason: QAC identifies the word as accusative predicate of the becoming verb, and form rows stress the plural active participle.

topics.headline: retrospective moral afterstate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears remorse rather than mere sadness: hidden calculation is recognized as error after exposure.
topics.reason: V4/root and CRITICAL rows connect regret with retrospective recognition and the concealment-to-exposure chain.

topics.headline: variant lightens sound, role remains stable
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the variant affects vocalic weight without changing the final predicate role.
topics.reason: The accepted variant is useful for contrast, but canonical grammar and role remain stable.

topics.headline: rare becoming-regret formula (5:31)
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes the final word as part of a rare becoming-regret formula, with 5:31 as the same-surah anchor.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows cite the formulaic pairing with the becoming root and the concrete 5:31 anchor.

topics.headline: final word lands the ayah on regret
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the ayah’s movement from disease, fear, and divine exposure land on regret, then press toward 5:53.
topics.reason: Structural and boundary rows identify the final word as closure and as setup for the next ayah.

topics.headline: uncertainty settles into remorse sound
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears earlier indefinite anxiety settle into the final remorse ending.
topics.reason: The sound row tracks the movement from earlier indefinite endings to the final plural participle ending.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The chain "in their hearts is sickness -> they hurry among them -> we fear that a turning calamity will strike us."
baseline_models.mechanism: An impaired inner center shortens deliberation and converts anticipated reversal into accelerated relational positioning. The feared outer turn and the unstable inner center reinforce one another: they seek security by moving early into the group imagined to survive the next turn.

activation_trace.role: The heart as the seat of understanding supplies the inner decision center whose condition governs the rush.
Weakening an affair and shortening movement makes the sickness function as impaired resolve rather than merely a medical label.
Speed contrary to slowness supplies the preemptive tempo of the attempted hedge.
The adverse circle or defeat supplies the anticipated reversal around which their positioning is organized.

changed_reading.before: They hurry into an affiliation because they prudently fear a future political setback.
changed_reading.after: Their haste is a symptom-producing hedge: inner disequilibrium makes a feared reversal govern present allegiance before any reversal occurs.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The verse separates "they say: we fear" from "what they concealed within themselves."
baseline_models.mechanism: Audible explanation and stored intention occupy different channels. The stated fear can be real without exhausting the motive; a concealed inner commitment remains available for later exposure, and regret attaches to that hidden store rather than only to a failed forecast.

activation_trace.role: Uttered speech supplies the public and inspectable rationale.
Concealment in the interior supplies a second channel that the spoken rationale does not disclose.
The inner domain of intention and discernment locates the concealed material as purposive inward content.
Regret over a missed or completed matter makes the concealed content the eventual object of retrospective judgment.

changed_reading.before: The sentence reports one motive, fear, followed by embarrassment when the prediction fails.
changed_reading.after: The sentence stages a split account: fear is what is said, while an unspoken allegiance or intention is what the resulting event makes regrettable.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The feared "circle" is answered by God bringing "the opening" or "a matter from with Him," after which they become regretful.
baseline_models.mechanism: Circular contingency keeps the hedge viable because outcomes can keep turning. An opening that also carries a judgment branch, or another divinely sourced matter, closes that optionality. The intervention does not merely improve one side's fortunes; it converts a reversible private strategy into an irreversible public condition.

activation_trace.role: Rotation and enclosure supply the repeatable orbit within which opportunistic positioning seems rational.
Resolving closure by judgment supplies a decisive reading of the opening that can terminate the orbit.
A matter, state, or affair keeps the alternative intervention broad while still making it a concrete change of conditions.
Nearness and presence mark the intervention's provenance as divine rather than as another move inside the human orbit.
Becoming a new state supplies the conversion from concealed strategy to settled consequence.

changed_reading.before: God may grant victory or send some other favorable event.
changed_reading.after: God may introduce adjudicative closure from outside the cycle, making a reversible hedge become a fixed and regrettable stance.

context_deltas.mechanism: The earlier self-facilitation, deed, attempted covering, and exact becoming-regret sequence turns the focus verse's hidden interior into a possible action-producing chamber. Concealment is not the end of the process: an externally supplied disclosure or lesson changes the actor's state and makes the hidden path legible as regret.

activation_trace.role: Interior concealment anchors the revised model in the focus verse's stored motive.
The self making an act easy supplies a mechanism by which inward content can facilitate outward conduct.
The inner domain of intention identifies the facilitating self as a purposive interior rather than a passive container.
Putting something behind visibility supplies the attempted covering stage between deed and recognition.
The shameful part that is covered supplies the concealed object's morally exposing character.
Becoming a state exactly matches the focus verse's transition formula and supplies the temporal conversion.
Regret over what has passed exactly matches the focus endpoint and makes the earlier sequence a causal template.

structural_cues: 5:30-31 moves from an inward self making a deed easy, through attempted covering, to "he became one of the regretful."
5:31 and 5:52 share the paired transition "became/become" plus "regretful."
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the self-facilitation and concealment-to-regret sequence plus the exact endpoint recurrence; I infer that the focus secret may likewise be action-facilitating and later exposed. A live alternative is that the recurrence marks only a shared result, not a shared causal path.

changed_reading.before: Their secret is a private belief that becomes embarrassing after an unexpected outcome.
changed_reading.after: Their secret may be the inward facilitation of their rush and affiliation; the later event functions as disclosure, moving them from managed concealment into recognized culpability.

context_deltas.mechanism: The earlier rush is embedded in a mouth-heart split and a selective intake rule: profess outwardly, listen through false channels, move words from their places, take a favorable ruling, and beware an unfavorable one. This sharpens the focus rush into tactical option-selection; the spoken fear is part of a public interface while the heart retains another operating rule.

activation_trace.role: The focus utterance supplies the public explanation to be tested against the earlier speech architecture.
The focus concealment supplies the private channel that the mouth-heart split activates.
The same speed branch places the focus haste inside an already described pattern of rapid movement.
Opening the mouth in speech supplies the outward profession that is explicitly detached from the heart.
The heart as understanding supplies the non-assenting interior and links directly to the focus's diseased hearts.
Falsehood supplies the corrupted information stream feeding the tactical rule.
Deviation from direction supplies the operation of moving words away from their settled orientation.
Taking and acquiring supplies the accept-if-favorable half of selective rule shopping.
Alert guarding against a feared result supplies the reject-if-unfavorable half of the same strategy.

structural_cues: 5:41 first names rushing, then contrasts profession by mouths with non-believing hearts.
Its quoted take-or-beware rule makes favorable-outcome selection an explicit behavior before 5:52's spoken risk rationale.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the repeated rush, mouth-heart split, distortion, and conditional take-or-beware speech; I infer one tactical architecture continuing into 5:52. A live alternative is that 5:41 and 5:52 describe overlapping but non-identical groups, so the architecture may be analogical rather than continuous.

changed_reading.before: The focus speakers simply state the danger that motivates their speed.
changed_reading.after: Their danger statement can function as the public layer of a selective strategy that seeks favorable channels while an unratified heart commitment remains concealed.

context_deltas.mechanism: The judgment sequence portrays authority already present yet abandoned, forbids people-directed fear and low-price exchange, bars following inclinations, frames plurality as a test, and contrasts uncertain preference with certain judgment. It activates the focus opening as adjudicative closure: a divine ruling exposes whether risk management or authoritative measure governed the hidden choice.

activation_trace.role: Judgment that resolves closure anchors the adjudicative reading in the focus word "opening."
Judgment between people supplies the authoritative measure that the actors solicit and then evade.
Presence with them supplies the paradox that access to authority does not ensure submission to it.
Turning away supplies the evasive response after an authoritative measure is available.
Fear with awe explicitly contrasts fear of people with fear of God and recalibrates the focus's stated fear.
Exchange supplies the transactional mechanism by which principle can be traded for perceived security.
Price in exchange supplies the low valuation assigned to authoritative signs under social pressure.
Following in sequence supplies the prohibited act of letting another guide displace the given measure.
Inclination of the self supplies the internal preference that competes with adjudication.
A test that makes condition visible supplies the diagnostic purpose of differing circumstances.
The repeated judgment branch makes the contrast between sought and divine judgment explicit.
Stable knowledge with doubt removed supplies the epistemic posture opposite fear-driven option shopping.

structural_cues: 5:43 juxtaposes a ruling already with them, seeking another arbitration, and turning away.
5:44-50 repeatedly returns to judging by what God sent, redirects fear, prohibits inclination-following, and closes with certainty.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the repeated judgment frame, fear contrast, exchange, test, inclination, and certainty; I infer that the focus's فتح can actualize its judgment branch and expose a risk-priced allegiance. Victory or simple relief remains a materially live reading of فتح alongside this adjudicative one.

changed_reading.before: The anticipated opening is an external success that proves the hedge mistaken.
changed_reading.after: The opening can be the authoritative decision that ends rule-shopping, reveals what the speakers priced above the divine measure, and makes their concealed risk calculus regrettable.

context_deltas.mechanism: The packet supplies two accelerated responses to uncertainty. Testing and eventual return direct one speed toward goods, whereas heart-sickness directs the focus speed into a protective group. Speed itself is therefore not the diagnosis; its object, governing fear, and expected destination distinguish faithful competition from opportunistic haste.

activation_trace.role: Speed contrary to slowness anchors the focus's accelerated movement.
A trial that reveals condition supplies uncertainty as a test rather than merely as a threat.
Advancing in a race supplies the packet's positively directed form of speed.
Inclination toward beneficial good supplies the race's object and moral direction.
Return to the origin supplies the common destination before which present movement is evaluated.

structural_cues: 5:48 commands racing toward goods under test and return; 5:52 depicts racing among a group under fear of reversal.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the two speed constructions and their different objects; I infer that they are contrastive orientations of agency. A live alternative is that the verbal forms mark only ordinary urgency and competition without an intended pair.

changed_reading.before: Haste is itself evidence of their sickness.
changed_reading.after: Haste becomes diagnostic only through its vector: they spend urgency on protective belonging instead of racing toward goods under the horizon of return.

context_deltas.mechanism: The adjacent verse reuses the striking-affliction root after turning away and assigns the prospective blow to some of their own wrongs. This folds the focus rationale back on itself: maneuvering to avoid being struck by a turn can participate in the turning-away that makes a divinely intended strike intelligible.

activation_trace.role: A calamity striking a person supplies the feared impact around which the focus hedge is narrated.
The adverse turn supplies the particular feared form of the strike.
Turning away supplies the prior directional act linked to the later affliction.
The same striking-calamity branch relocates impact from an uncontrolled political turn to a consequence God may intend.
Sin supplies the moral source attached to the second striking event.

structural_cues: 5:49 says God may intend to strike them for some sins; 5:52 quotes fear that a turning calamity may strike us.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the close lexical echo and the turning-away/sin frame; I infer an ironic rebound in which avoidance behavior helps produce culpability. The two strikes could instead remain separate warnings with no causal fold between them.

changed_reading.before: Their policy seeks to insure against an external calamity.
changed_reading.after: The insurance policy may invert into exposure: fear of being struck motivates a turn that places their own conduct under another, morally sourced striking.

context_deltas.mechanism: The immediate frame defines one mutual protection network before the focus and another allegiance network after it, ending in a cohesive party's overcoming. The rush "among them" is thus a bid to cross into a self-supporting solidarity under anticipated reversal; the sequel contests the premise by relocating protection and victory.

activation_trace.role: Rapid movement supplies the attempted entry into a protective relational field.
Love, support, and alliance supply the mutual network immediately antecedent to "among them."
Parts and constituent groups supply the reciprocal "some of them with some" structure of that network.
Supportive allegiance supplies the counter-location of protection after the focus.
Taking supportive allegiance supplies the act that forms the alternative coalition.
A group cohering around one view supplies the resulting organized party.
Overcoming force supplies the outcome that the focus speakers tried to secure through the rival network.

structural_cues: 5:51 defines mutual awliya, 5:52 says they hurry "among them," and 5:55-56 redefine wali and the overcoming party.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the enclosing walaya sequence and the focus pronoun; I infer that the rush is attempted incorporation into a protection network. The exact social and legal scope of walaya remains open and is not settled by this mechanism.

changed_reading.before: They cultivate useful allies in case power changes hands.
changed_reading.after: They race to relocate belonging into a mutually protective network, but the surrounding sequence contests both where protection resides and which coalition actually overcomes.

context_deltas.mechanism: The immediate sequel places emphatic sworn solidarity beside collapsed deeds and another becoming-state formula. This makes the focus secret socially consequential: public assurances of being "with you" can coexist with a concealed alternative commitment until the opening turns words and works into an observable loss.

activation_trace.role: Concealed inward content anchors the gap between solidarity claims and operative commitment.
An oath apportioned to its parties supplies the formal public assurance of solidarity.
The sworn oath supplies the assurance's emphatic binding form.
Falling and decline supply the collapse of the position built through those assurances.
Purposive deeds supply what is nullified, extending exposure beyond speech to enacted strategy.
Becoming a new state repeats the focus transition from concealed posture to public result.
Commercial loss supplies the failed return on their strategic investment.

structural_cues: 5:53 immediately asks about those who swore maximal oaths that they were with you, then says their deeds collapsed and they became losers.
The focus and 5:53 both use becoming to mark a settled post-disclosure state.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the immediate oath, collapse, and becoming-loss sequence; I infer that the focus secret concerns divided solidarity expressed through conduct. A live alternative is that 5:53 reports believers' discovery without specifying the full content of what 5:52 says was concealed.

changed_reading.before: The concealed matter is an unspecified private thought that later causes remorse.
changed_reading.after: The concealed matter can be a divided commitment hidden beneath maximal solidarity claims, with the opening exposing both the claim and the works built around it as loss.

context_deltas.mechanism: The next movement answers defection with God bringing another people whose fear structure is opposite: they act without fearing blame and receive divine bounty. The focus's "God may bring" can therefore include social replacement as the form taken by opening or matter, not only an impersonal event.

activation_trace.role: Coming and arrival anchor the focus intervention in a verb repeated by the replacement sequence.
Apostasy and turning back supply the vacancy to which the incoming people respond.
The coming branch supplies the exact divine-arrival echo that introduces replacement, alongside the root's later giving occurrence.
A people or human collective supplies the social embodiment of what God brings.
Expected-harm fear, explicitly negated here, supplies the contrast to the focus speakers' governing anticipation.
Blame for what merits reproach supplies the social pressure that the incoming people do not fear.

context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the repeated divine-coming syntax, defection, incoming people, and reversed fear posture; I infer that replacement can instantiate the anticipated opening. A live alternative is that 5:54 describes a later analogous response rather than the same event anticipated in 5:52.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it carries bodily branches of sickness and circular dizziness into political judgment. It remains anchored in the focus's seeing, sickness, circle, and opening, and it explains haste as disoriented stabilization. Downstream prose should present it only as a somatic analogy, not replace the ordinary adverse-turn sense of دائرة.

activation_trace.role: Visual and insightful perception supplies the diagnostic viewpoint from which disorientation can be recognized.

Dizziness of the head supplies the felt instability that can provoke a rush for immediate support.

changed_reading.before: They rationally scan a rotating field and move toward the safest side.
changed_reading.after: Their inner loss of clarity makes the field feel vertiginous; the rush is an attempt to stop that dizziness, while the opening restores enough clarity to see the move as regrettable.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates the disputed antithetical branch in which أسر can denote making manifest. The exact focus form, opening, seeing, and later becoming keep the activation anchored, but downstream prose should call it lexical irony or branch resonance, never a forced replacement translation of "concealed."
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The sequence from ترى through الفتح to ما أسروا and فيصبحوا.

activation_trace.role: The contested manifestation sense inside the concealment root supplies the secret's latent tendency to become public.
Causing something to be seen supplies the verse's diagnostic exposure vector.
Unclosing and disclosure by insight supplies the event that releases the secret's manifest side.
Becoming a settled condition supplies the conversion from hidden content to observable consequence.

changed_reading.before: A wholly hidden motive remains private until an external victory happens.
changed_reading.after: The hidden motive carries an ironic manifest edge: the opening does not invent its exposure but completes a movement already latent in the verse's conceal/show tension.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is a branch-distant material analogy: the harmful-swelling image of حبط is mapped onto emphatic oath display. It remains validly anchored by the focus's concealed interior and the immediate oath-collapse-becoming sequence. Downstream prose should qualify it as an image of inflated exteriority, not as the lexical meaning of the 5:53 verb.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: ما أسروا في أنفسهم followed immediately by maximal oaths, collapsed works, and another becoming-state.

activation_trace.role: A hidden interior supplies what the emphatic exterior fails to represent.
A formal oath supplies the public shell of asserted solidarity.
Sworn force supplies the shell's emphatic inflation.
Swelling from harmful intake supplies the cross-domain image of an enlarged exterior with a damaging interior.
Becoming a new state supplies the shell's collapse into publicly settled loss.

changed_reading.before: Their assurances are simply falsified when events change.
changed_reading.after: Their maximal assurances can be pictured as an inflated shell around a damaging concealed commitment; disclosure collapses the enlargement and leaves the actual loss visible.

strongest_changes: The 5:30-31 self-facilitation, covering, and exact becoming-regret recurrence turns the focus secret from passive thought into a possible action-producing interior.
The 5:41 mouth-heart and take-or-beware sequence makes the spoken fear part of tactical option-selection rather than a complete account of motive.
The 5:43-50 judgment sequence activates فتح as adjudicative closure that exposes a fear-priced allegiance.
The 5:51-56 walaya frame makes the rush a bid for protective incorporation, while the repeated divine-coming syntax opens a replacement reading.
summary.what_was_special: The packet repeatedly changes the same focus mechanisms rather than merely adding topics: two kinds of speed, two striking afflictions, two becoming-state endpoints, rival protection networks, and a divine-coming echo all converge on how concealed risk management becomes exposed.
remaining_uncertainties: فتح can retain victory, relief, and opening senses alongside adjudicative closure; the trace does not choose one.
The exact content of what was concealed is not stated, so divided allegiance remains an abductive reconstruction.
The people brought in 5:54 may instantiate the event anticipated in 5:52 or may be a later analogous replacement.
The somatic, antithetical-secret, and oath-inflation readings require explicit exploratory qualification.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Fear of a turning cycle drives premature alignment.** `د و ر B004` is an adverse turn, `س ر ع B001` quickness, and `م ر ض B004` a weakened affair. The packet supplies feared reversal and hurried movement. I infer that inward imbalance converts uncertainty into opportunistic speed.
2. **Opening exposes the hidden core.** `ف ت ح B008` is inward opening/disclosure and `س ر ر B001` hidden inwardness. The anticipated opening or command leads to morning exposure and remorse (`ن د م B001`). I infer that victory opens not only circumstances but concealed motives.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Later ayah 5:120 made the fixed ayah's local distinctions newly visible as bounded operations within a single encompassing dominion, rather than as an isolated rule or episode.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Fear of a turn produces anticipatory orbiting.** Fixed **د و ر / B003** (“circulation of states and handling of affairs”) and **B004** (“an adverse turn, misfortune, or defeat”) give *dāʾirah* both cyclical change and feared loss. The agents rush into an alliance to stay near whichever side may prevail; the ayah then posits an opening or command that reverses their calculation and exposes the hidden motive. I infer that fear converts uncertain political circulation into compulsive repositioning. Their haste reads as an attempt to orbit fortune, not principled loyalty.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 5:53 made the hidden calculation collapse into visible loss, and 5:54’s incoming replacement showed that orbiting fortune cannot secure communal function.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, görmeyi hem gözle algılama hem de gözün işlevine benzetilen içsel kavrayış olarak kuruyor. Doğrudan göz tanıklığı bu çekirdeğin duyusal gerçekleşimidir; zihinsel görüş, uyku düşü ve başkalarına görünme amacı bu dalın dışında kalır.
